newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico private consumption seen up in 97 - Ortiz.
newsitem.headline: Mexico private consumption seen up in 97 - Ortiz.

text.p: Private sector consumption in Mexico is seen growing a real 2.5 percent next year after growing 2.1 percent this year, Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said in a radio interview Friday.
Ortiz said the increase was "not an enormous expansion," but added that it nevertheless represented a "significant recovery" from Mexico's economic slump of 1995.
Ortiz told Radio Red in a morning interview that one of the main aims of the government's 1997 economic programme was to ensure that the economic recovery becomes more broadly based.
For this to happen, it remained essential that the macro-economic targets continue to be hit, he added.
He predicted that 1997 would bring a consolidation of the recovery begun in 1996 and a recovery in purchasing power -- certainly not to 1994 levels, but nevertheless an "advance".

Ortiz also said the international environment looked favourable for Mexico in 1997, with the United States likely to see growth of 2.5 to 3.0 percent with low inflation and growth also picking up in Europe and Japan.
